notes:
- **Search inside screenshots, the second Pro feature.** With Pro, the strip's search box (**Ctrl+F** or **/**) also finds a capture by the words *in* the picture, an error message, an order number, a name, as well as by file name, app and window title. A capture that matched by its words shows a one-line **snippet** under its name, with what you typed in Volt (`…payment for Order 4417 failed…`), and the same line in its tooltip. Without Pro nothing is read; a search that finds nothing adds **Search the words inside screenshots with Pro**, which opens the Pro sheet.
- **Read on your PC, in the background.** After each capture is saved, a low-priority worker reads its text with the same on-device Windows text recognition Alt+X uses; it never runs on the capture's clock. Captures from before Pro was on are read gradually, newest first, a few a minute (faster when the PC is left alone), until the folder is covered. An edited capture is read again after you save it; a deleted one leaves the index and **Undo** reads it again. Secure captures are never read or indexed.
- **Where the words are kept.** In `.a9snap\text.json` inside your screenshots folder, next to `captures.json` and the edit originals, keyed by file name, size and time so an edited or replaced file never carries old words. **They are text from your screenshots**: they stay on this PC, never go in the log and are never sent anywhere. **Saving > Search inside screenshots** (a Pro badge without Pro) turns the reading on or off, shows how far it is (**Read 412 of 1,280 captures**, then **All captures read**), and **Clear text index** deletes the words after asking. Turning it off stops reading and deletes the index.
- The **Pro features** page lists Search inside screenshots as **Included**, with how to use it and a **How to use** link. The manual's strip, Settings, Pro features and Privacy pages cover it.
